docs.title: Scratch Arcade Quest
docs.text:
Build a bright, fast little Scratch platform game over four lessons. The style is inspired by classic 16-bit arcade platformers: a hero runs, jumps, grabs coins, dodges enemies, and reaches a flag at the end of the level.

Each lesson is designed for independent work. Start at Lesson 1 and continue to work through the lessons.

docs.title: What You Will Make
docs.text:
By the end, your game will include:

  • A controllable hero sprite.
  • Platforms and jump physics.
  • Coins, score, and sound effects.
  • Enemies, lives, and a game over moment.
  • A finish flag, timer, and win screen.

docs.title: What You Need
docs.text:
• Scratch open in the desktop app.
  • A new project named Arcade Quest.
  • A hero sprite, a coin sprite, an enemy sprite, and a flag sprite.
  • A simple platform backdrop drawn with solid ground colors.

docs.title: How To Use The Code Images
docs.text: Scratch code examples are shown as block images. Copy the blocks into Scratch one at a time.

docs.title: Start
docs.text: Start Lesson 1, Task 1: Draw Your Hero

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Make the character the player will control.

docs.title: Do This
docs.text:
1. Open Scratch desktop.
  2. Delete the cat sprite.
  3. Click Choose a Sprite.
  4. Click Paint.
  5. Draw a small arcade hero.
  6. Rename the sprite Player.

docs.text:

  2. Click Backdrops.
  3. Draw blue sky.
  4. Draw green ground along the bottom.
  5. Draw two floating block-style platforms.
  6. Keep the platform top colour the same green each time.

docs.title: Level Up: Make The Screen Move
Goal
docs.text: Make the level move sideways when the player walks right.

docs.title: What This Means
docs.text:
The Scratch Stage does not really move.

Instead, the Player stays near the middle of the screen, and the level sprites move left.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
Make a new scene for this Level Up.

  1. Click the Stage thumbnail.
  2. Click Backdrops.
  3. Click Choose a Backdrop.
  4. Click Paint.
  5. Rename the new backdrop Scrolling Level.
  6. Draw the sky and background.
  7. Do not draw platforms on this backdrop.

For this Level Up, the platforms must be sprites so they can move.

  1. Click Choose a Sprite.
  2. Click Paint.
  3. Draw one green rectangle platform.
  4. Rename it Platform 1.
  5. Right-click Platform 1.
  6. Click duplicate.
  7. Rename the copy Platform 2.
  8. Right-click Platform 2.
  9. Click duplicate.
  10. Rename the copy Platform 3.
  11. Put the three platforms across the new scene.

docs.title: Do This
docs.text:
1. Click Variables.
  2. Click Make a Variable.
  3. Name the variable scroll x.
  4. Click OK.
  5. In the sprite list below the Stage, click the Player sprite. (If you cannot remember where the sprite list is, go back to Start Here: Where To Click Sprites.)
  6. Add switch backdrop to Scrolling Level under the green flag block.
  7. Build the rest of this code.

docs.title: Change The Number
docs.text:
The code image uses 0.

For each sprite, change the 0 to the number below:

  • Platform 1: use 0
  • Platform 2: use 240
  • Platform 3: use 480
  • Coin: use 300
  • Enemy: use 520
  • Flag: use 700

Build the same code on Platform 2, Platform 3, Coin, Enemy, and Flag.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
When the player walks right, the platforms, coins, enemy, and flag should move left.

The player should look like they are travelling through a longer level.
